paragraphs.text: Both of you are now retired, and you have confirmed that your objectives and circumstances remain unchanged since our last review. You are comfortable with maintaining the balanced approach to risk previously agreed.
You do not require any income from the portfolio at present.
Your risk profile remains at a level 5 balanced.
We propose you invest the full value of your joint General Investment Account.
The funds will come from the joint General Investment Account.
We recommend topping up both David's and Susan's Stocks & Shares ISAs.
This recommendation involves selling your existing investments.

It was agreed to disinvest the joint General Investment Account in full and use the proceeds to top up both of your Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year, splitting the proceeds equally between the two ISAs.
It was also agreed to disinvest the joint GIA in full and split the proceeds equally between both ISAs for the new tax year.
The proceeds will be funded from the joint General Investment Account.
Selling down the General Investment Account constitutes a disposal and may give rise to a capital gains position that will need to be considered and assessed against your annual exempt amount.
